original_test_intent: Inject one uncorrectable ECC event through every in-scope memory controller, verify the event is attributed to the correct physical DIMM/controller across OS, BMC and recovered UEFI, confirm the front-panel response, and recover the isolated SUT without persistent corruption.
original_method: An FAE/operator maps memory controllers to socket/channel/DIMM/sub-channel/rank tuples, enables the approved BIOS controls, performs one UCE injection per authorized controller, monitors any crash on an independent console, gathers full pre-crash and recovered evidence plus indicator state, follows the vendor recovery path and restores settings. Controller and rank coverage are approved before execution.
manual_activity: The FAE/operator must translate controller coverage into exact tuples, configure and restore BIOS, inject one UCE per approved controller, observe the fault lamp and govern crash recovery. Agent cannot choose a destructive memory target.
required_inputs: Supported Intel ITP/CScripts build/hash and UCE consumption/target semantics
Per-controller coverage matrix including whether rank 0 is sufficient
Authoritative Windows/BMC/recovered-UEFI UCE fields and indicator applicability
Crash timeout, console/backup/recovery and post-recovery memory/data-integrity checks
safety_requirements: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, console, configuration/data backup and FAE approval
Preserve existing evidence instead of clearing logs
Validate each destructive tuple against the controller and physical slot
One injection only per approved target; stop on wrong attribution, uncontrolled MCE, crash beyond plan or data-integrity concern
No automatic retry; restore settings and prove boot/memory health before another target
agent_execution_scope: Capture approved inventory/topology and read-only OS/BMC/UEFI evidence before and after recovery
Do not enter BIOS, select a memory tuple, inject UCE, reset/power-cycle, repeat or assign PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve controller-to-tuple/rank coverage and package semantics
Define expected severity, crash behavior and exact slot/controller fields per evidence plane
Resolve Windows evidence source and indicator/UEFI applicability
Approve recovery, integrity verification, restoration and final verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The SSH tail is partial post-event evidence, assumes dmesg despite Windows, cannot prove the selected memory controller or rank, may be unavailable after UCE crash and omits UEFI/front-panel/recovery proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Keep the exact FAE-operated `injectMemError(..., rank=0, errType="uce")` only for an approved controller tuple; use authoritative Windows/BMC/UEFI read-only exports for evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: UCE, fixed rank 0, Memory controller 1~N and 15/10-minute estimates remain literal; no tuple or crash behavior is guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind every controller to captured `mc.dimminfo()` and service-label evidence, execute one UCE per approved target under an outage monitor, correlate address/controller/slot across all logs, record physical indication and perform vendor recovery plus memory/filesystem integrity checks and BIOS diff.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds deterministic controller coverage and post-crash integrity evidence while preserving the UCE stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic uncorrected-error line cannot prove controller 1~N coverage or correct physical attribution; absence of recovery evidence misses the destructive outcome.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: UCE may crash the OS, corrupt in-flight data, poison memory state or leave the system unbootable; wrong tuples affect unintended DIMMs.

project_override_considerations: The user/FAE and package gates make a controlled future run possible but do not grant autonomous destructive authority. Missing topology/recovery blocks execution, not the review or DUT verdict.
expected_evidence: Package hash, full `mc.dimminfo()` and controller-to-tuple/rank coverage matrix
Per-controller injection transcript and synchronized crash/recovery timeline
Authoritative Windows UCE/MCE, BMC SEL and recovered UEFI SEL naming the same controller/slot
Front-panel evidence, BIOS restoration, memory/data-integrity and health checks, engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items require Memory controller 1~N, but the command targets a DIMM tuple at fixed rank 0 without an iteration/coverage map. Windows is booted while dmesg is required, and UEFI/front-panel criteria use undefined `if there is one` applicability.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The UCE operation and desired fatal attribution are identifiable; an FAE package, topology matrix and recovery contract can resolve readiness. Execution remains gated, but the case is not irreducibly blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 14 Wistron-System RAS-00734-V003: approve the memory-controller 1~N to socket/channel/DIMM/sub-channel/rank/physical-slot map, Intel ITP/CScripts version/hash and `errType="uce"` semantics; define whether rank=0 tuples cover each controller, bounded count and expected crash; reconcile Windows with dmesg; specify mandatory BMC/UEFI/front-panel evidence, backup, recovery, integrity checks and BIOS restoration.

review_improvement: The review prevents one DIMM-tuple UCE from being counted as all-controller coverage and adds the recovery/data-integrity evidence demanded by this row's destructive severity.
independent_technical_reasoning: A memory-controller label is a higher-level coverage unit than the injector's DIMM tuple. Multiple channels, sub-channels and ranks may share a controller, so a rank-0 event proves only the approved mapping, not automatically the whole controller or all controllers. UCE can terminate Windows before host-side collection, making the independent BMC/console timeline and recovered UEFI record essential. Because the source explicitly boots Windows, a Windows RAS/WHEA oracle must replace assumed dmesg. These are resolvable engineering prerequisites, supporting REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION rather than BLOCKED.
